title: Markets move on the bet, not the announcement
hook: The Fed raised rates exactly as expected — so why did nothing move?
metaphor: It is like a match everyone already knows the score of. The betting happens for weeks. The final whistle changes nothing.
body: Traders bet on Fed decisions weeks ahead of the meeting.
Prices adjust as those odds shift, long before the day arrives.
If the decision matches the bet, prices often barely move.
The surprise is what moves money, not the announcement itself.

live.template: For the next meeting on {next_fomc}, the market prices about {hike}% odds of a rise and {hold}% odds of no change.

caveat: These odds come from futures prices and move every day. They are a live bet, not a forecast.
